title: Palworld element type effectiveness chart
notes: Project owner provided the type chart and multiplier rules directly. Super effective = 2x, not very effective = 0.5x, neutral = 1x. Dual-type targets multiply both multipliers. No game DataTable contains a standalone type chart; this is a game-mechanics rule.

title: Paldb Pal pages with spawner cards (English)
notes: Fan-maintained database; the archived snapshots carry a site footer of v1.0.4 dated 2026/09/07. Each Pal page was read for its Spawner card: FishingSpot_* rows mean fishing-only, Raid rows mean raid-only, and pages without a Spawner card mean no wild spawn. Pages whose spawner card is absent or lists no spawner are recorded as reviewed_absent; pages that list fixed world spawn points were resolved separately from project owner clarifications.

title: Project owner clarifications for Pals with no reviewed field spawner
notes: Project owner reviewed the Pals that no target-build spawner table places and ruled: Dandilord and Silvance spawn from tribe strongholds (Rotmist Root and Shinespore Root, Lv 78); Panthalus is the boss of Deserted Islet (Lv 70); Xenovader never appears on the map directly and only has a chance to appear through the meteor event that spawns randomly in every region except Sakurajima; Astralym cannot be captured. The owner also confirmed that Panthalus, Astralym, and Moon Lord have no work suitability, so an empty work list is correct rather than missing data.

title: Palworld Wiki (wiki.gg) Wooden Club and Bat item pages
notes: The Wooden Club page carries the target-build Bat row description, Technology level 1, Attack 25, and a Wood x5 recipe; the Bat page carries the target-build Bat2 row description, Technology level 7, Attack 50, and a Wood x30 plus Stone x10 recipe. Paldb (Wooden_Club code Bat, Bat code Bat2) states the same split, so the duplicate English name "Bat" was a localization read error on the Bat row, not two items sharing a name by design.

title: Palworld Wiki (wiki.gg) Elements page
notes: Nine elements; each element is strong against zero to two others and weak against exactly one. The strong-against list is Dark to Neutral, Dragon to Dark, Electric to Water, Fire to Grass and Ice, Ground to Electric, Grass to Ground, Ice to Dragon, Water to Fire, and Neutral to none, which is exactly the nine reviewed type_effectiveness edges. Every other attacking and defending pair is neutral 1x by design rather than missing data.

title: Project owner clarifications for raid Pals with no breeding rank
notes: Project owner ruled that True Eye of Cthulhu can be produced by pairing two of its own species and that Moon Lord cannot be captured, so it is never a breeding parent or a formula child. Both Pals therefore have no combi rank or priority in the target build rather than missing values.

title: Paldb item Production cards (English)
notes: Each item page's Production card lists every station that can craft that item, which is the only station evidence available for the 767 recipes whose crafted item and unlocking schematic descriptions state no crafting sentence. The card order is not a tier order: Cloth lists High Quality Workbench before Primitive Workbench, while Makeshift Handgun lists Weapon Workbench first. The reviewer therefore ranked the listed stations by build tier and took the lowest one, which is the same rule the 518 text-resolved recipes follow, and spot-checked that match on Cloth, Carbon Fiber, Cement, Recovery Meds, Bellanoir's Slab, the Makeshift weapons, Flour, Charcoal, Ingot, Refined Ingot, Pal Metal Ingot, and Plastic. Station display names follow the target build's DT_MapObjectNameText rows. 32 recipes whose recorded station was not the lowest listed one were corrected: Makeshift Weapon Factory to Weapon Workbench, Laboratory to Primitive Workbench, Medicine Workbench to Medieval Medicine Workbench, Flour Mill to Mill, and Furnace to Primitive Furnace, Improved Furnace, or Electric Furnace by ingot tier.
